question.knowledge_point: Solving a System of Equations Given an Augmented Matrix Containing Non-Unit Leading Entries
question.problem:
Solve the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned} & {x}_{1}+5{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=-1 \\  & -{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}=7 \\  & 2{x}_{3}=4\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
The third equation states that 

$$
2{x}_{3}=4\,⟹\,{x}_{3}=2.
$$

 Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
-{x}_{2}+3(2)=7\,⟹\,{x}_{2}=6-7=-1.
$$

Now, we substitute ${x}_{3}=2$ and ${x}_{2}=-1$ into the first equation to get

$$
{x}_{1}+5(-1)+(2)=-1\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-1+5-2=2.
$$

Therefore, the solution is 
${x}_{1}=2$, ${x}_{2}=-1$, and ${x}_{3}=2.$  In vector form, the solution can be written as $[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

question.knowledge_point: Solving a System of Equations Given an Augmented Matrix Containing Non-Unit Leading Entries
question.problem:
Solve the system of equations represented by the augmented matrix: 

$$
[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$
question.worked_solution:
The matrix represents a system of three linear equations in three variables, say, $x$, $y$, and $z.$ We obtain the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned} & 4x+y+2z=-3 \\  & y+3z=0 \\  & -z=1\end{aligned}
$$

The third equation states that 

$$
-z=1\,⟹\,z=-1.
$$

Substituting this into the second equation, we get

$$
y+3(-1)=0\,⟹\,y=3.
$$

Now, we substitute $z=-1$ and $y=3$ into the first equation to get

$$
4x+(3)+2(-1)=-3\,⟹\,x=\frac{-3-3+2}{4}=-1.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=-1$, $y=3$, and $z=-1.$ In vector form, the solution can be written as 
$[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$

question.knowledge_point: Finding Unions and Intersections of Finite Families of Indexed Sets
question.worked_solution:
The union of a family of indexed sets is the set containing all elements belonging to *at least one* set in the indexed family:

$$
{⋃}_{i\in I}{A}_{i}=\{x\in U\,:\,x\in {A}_{i}\,\,\text{for at least one }{A}_{i},\,\,i\in I\}
$$

where $U$ is a universal set.

Therefore, in our case, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{⋃}_{i\in I}{S}_{i} & ={S}_{0}\cup {S}_{1}\cup {S}_{2} \\  & =\{0\}\,\cup \,(0,1)\,\cup \,(0,2) \\  & =[0,2).\end{aligned}
$$

$$

question.knowledge_point: Finding Unions and Intersections of (Countably) Infinite Families of Indexed Sets
question.worked_solution:
The intersection of a family of indexed sets $\{{A}_{i}\}_{i\in I}$ contains all elements that belong to *all* sets in our family:

$$
{⋂}_{i\in I}{A}_{i}=\{x\in U\,:\,x\in {A}_{i}\,\,\text{for all }{A}_{i},\,\,i\in I\}
$$

where $U$ is a universal set.

Let's now write down a few instances of our indexed sets:

- if $i=-1,$ we have ${X}_{-1}=\{-2,-1\}$

- if $i=0,$ we have ${X}_{0}=\{-1,0\}$

- if $i=1,$ we have ${X}_{1}=\{0,1\}$

and so on. 

Notice that there is no element that belongs to all the sets. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{⋂}_{i\in I}{X}_{i}=∅.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

By applying elementary row operations of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{2},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary row operations?
question.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries above and below ${a}_{21}=-1$ equal to $0.$

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-7 & 4 & 3 \\ -1 & 2 & 2 \\ -8 & 6 & 4\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-7{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & -10 & -11 \\ -1 & 2 & 2 \\ -8 & 6 & 4\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-8{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & -10 & -11 \\ -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & -10 & -12\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-7{R}_{2}\,$ and $\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-8{R}_{2}.$

A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 & 1 \\ 3 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-7 & -6 & 2 \\ -2 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

By applying elementary column operations of the form ${C}_{i}:={C}_{i}+k{C}_{3},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the elementary column operations?
question.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries to the left of ${a}_{33}=1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 & 1 \\ 3 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-3{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-7 & 2 & 2 \\ -2 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-4{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-7 & -6 & 2 \\ -2 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary column operations are

$\,$ ${C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-3{C}_{3}\,$ and $\,{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-4{C}_{3}.$
